notes: Minifigure assembly (caps, heads, torsos, legs, hips) is shown but those parts are not in the parts list, so they are not recorded.
The 2x wand sub-assembly is read as a trans-neon-green 1x1 cone on a light bluish gray lightsaber hilt (lego-23306). The minifigs hold them in their hands, which is not recorded.
Step 1 is a 6x10 grey plate. Step 2 puts six red 2x2 seats on it, and each seat is listed as resting on the plate. Exact positions are not recorded.

Page 3 has two separate sub-builds. The left one is a seat row (b12–b20) and the right one is a small desk or counter (b21–b28). The seat row's seats are the third and fourth rows' worth of seats the set needs.

Seat row: the three black C-shaped pieces in step 2 are read as lego-3680 turntable bases, because three are left in the parts list. The three back seats are placed on them and the two front seats go directly on the plate. This is uncertain.

Desk: the yellow part is read as lego-43337, the 1x4 thick-wall panel. The two white striped parts are read as lego-2412b grille tiles. The blue parts are read as 1x2 plates. Step 3 appears to show the yellow part larger, but it is probably the same piece seen from another angle, so I added nothing for it.
The white inverted slope (lego-3747b) in step 3 is shown floating at the back-right of the plate. It is listed as resting on the plate only.
Exact placement of the desk's small plates is a best reading of the drawing.
The 'remaining parts' lists cross-check page 3: its counts match the pieces I placed there.

Steps 4 and 5 continue the desk on the right plate b21. Step 4 adds two light bluish gray 75° slopes (lego-4460a) beside the grille tiles. Step 4 also adds a tall white block that I read as a lego-3245b on the white inverted slope b28. Step 5 adds a blue plate across the tops, a red seat on the front of the plate, and a black bag on the yellow panel.
The blue top is read as a 1x6 plate (lego-3666) and the tall white block as a lego-3245b. Both are uncertain.
The black bag is listed as resting on the yellow panel b23. It is probably only placed there, not fastened.

The yellow inset (steps 1–4) builds a small coffee machine. It uses a grey 2x2x2 box with two black hinge bricks as wheels at its base, a trans-neon green cone inside, a trans-clear door, a white grille tile and a white side-handle plate on top, and two clear goblets on the plate's studs. Step 6 sets it into the gap between the slopes, on the grille tiles b25 and b26.
The two black hinge bricks (b36, b37) are shown at the bottom of the box. I could not tell exactly how they attach, so they are listed with no resting piece.

This page builds a cockpit pilot-seat module on a new 6x10 plate (b44). The inventory counts from the 'not yet placed' lists agree with page 4's pieces. Only some of this page's pieces can be cross-checked that way.

Step 2: the blue row is read as the 1x6 blue brick lego-3009 and the red piece as a 1x2 red brick. The grey block is read as the 32530 pin connector plate, with the grey 30377 arm acting as the joystick. Step 3 adds a blue inverted slope (3660) on top. This reading is uncertain.

Step 4 shows two white 45° control-panel slopes (3039pr0013 and 3039pr0002) beside the blue slope, plus two red seats on the plate. Step 5 adds a dark bluish gray 3x6 wedge plate over the slopes and the blue slope, and two white 1x2x2 bricks on the plate.
Step 6 (2x): a black brick with side studs (52107) goes on each white 1x2x2 brick. A white grille tile is pressed onto the side stud of each. The tiles rest on nothing below.

The left half of page 6 shows steps 5 and 6 of the same cockpit module as page 5, with the numbering restarting. It adds the monitor tile (3068bpr0137, b61) on the right-hand block and a white 1x4 arch (3659, b62) bridging the two black-topped blocks. The remaining-parts diff supports this, because the arch and monitor were not used earlier. How the monitor attaches is uncertain.

The right half starts a new sub-model, a small yellow cart with a sign. Step 1: the yellow 4x6 plate is shown upside down, with two black 1x4 wheel-holder plates (2926) fitted to its underside. Step 2: a black 2x2 pin-hole plate goes on top, after the plate is flipped. Step 3: a grey antenna goes on the black plate and two dark grey 33° 3x1 slopes go on the yellow plate.
The wheel holders are listed as resting on the yellow plate b63. Wheels are not added yet.
The antenna pole is read as lego-3957a. It sits on the black 2x2 plate.
The 'remaining parts' lists back up page 6's pieces. This page's pieces cannot be checked that way.

Inset steps 1–2: a dark grey hinge cylinder (30553) is slid onto the finger of a yellow 1x2 hinge plate (44567a). The yellow plate's studs are then pressed under the black stairs (30134, shown upside down).
Step 4: the stairs assembly sits on the cart, with the stairs on the two grey slopes. The antenna rod enters the hinge cylinder, which makes a swivel post and lets the stair platform lift.

Step 6: four wheels (8x6 hub plus 14x4 tyre) are added to the black wheel-holder plates, and a yellow panel (43337) goes on the platform. I am unsure which yellow piece the sign tile is. The 'LC 7893' sticker from sheet 55075 is applied to it, and I did not record the sticker as a part.
The wheel hubs are listed with no resting piece and joined to the wheel-holder plates, with each tyre resting on its hub.
Page 8 starts booklet 2, the airplane. The fuselage floor is five light bluish gray curved inverted 8x8x2 bricks (54091) chained end to end with pairs of black Technic pins.

Step 1 shows the first section with two pins going into the end holes. In step 2 each following section is joined to the previous one by two pins, 10 pins in all (the remaining-parts list has 20 pins). That is my reading of the arrows, so which section carries which pins is a best guess.
The 'remaining parts' lists back up page 7: four wheels, four tyres, the stairs, the hinge cylinder, the yellow hinge plate and the yellow panel are all consumed.
The 'remaining parts' lists back up page 8, because exactly 10 Technic pins and the 5 curved inverted bricks were consumed.

Step 3 shows the whole fuselage chain from b82 (left, pins visible at its far end) to b86 (right), with a white nose attached to the b86 end. The nose is read as the printed forward fuselage 54092c01pr0001, and its side flaps are assumed to be part of that piece.

Ballast bricks sit on the stud floor of the chain: red 2x2 in section 1, yellow 2x4 in section 2, a red 1x2 and a red 1x2 at the section 3/4 boundary, yellow 2x4 in section 4, and red 2x2 in section 5. Which section each brick sits in is read from the picture's spacing.
I am not sure that the nose is 54092c01pr0001 rather than a pair of 54096 slopes.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 9: nose b97, red 2x2s, red 1x2s and yellow 2x4 bricks are gone from the list.
Step 4 adds eight yellow 1x2 grooved tiles in pairs on the wall ledges at the four section joints, so each joint is covered by two tiles that rest on the two neighbouring sections.
Each yellow 2x4 brick gets two blue 1x2 plates laid across its width. These are read as lego-3023 blue, and the colour and type are a best guess.
At the nose end, a yellow 2x5 block next to the red 2x2 is read as a 2x3 plate plus a 2x2 plate, resting on the last section and the nose. It could instead be one 2x6 plate (lego-3795).
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 10: eight yellow 1x2 tiles, four blue 1x2 plates, one yellow 2x3 plate and one yellow 2x2 plate are gone.

Step 5 puts a yellow 2x2 plate over each pair of blue 1x2 plates on the two yellow 2x4 bricks. At the nose end, the yellow 2x5 block is mostly covered by a 2x4 plate that leaves one yellow stud column showing.
I could not tell which plate covers the nose-end block. I used the light bluish gray 2x4 (lego-3020) because the visible studs look grey-white, so that colour and type are a guess.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 11: two yellow 2x2 plates and one light bluish gray 2x4 plate are consumed.

Inset steps 1–2 build the aft section 54701c01pr0001 with two stacks, each two red round 2x2 plates, as ballast. A yellow 2x2 plate caps each stack. Step 6 joins the aft section to the pin end of the first chain section (b82).

Parts-count conflict: all three yellow lego-3022 plates were already used on pages 10–11, so the two yellow 2x2s here cannot be 3022 by the parts list. I used 3022 anyway. The drawing shows 2x2 yellow squares, and the true type may be another yellow part from the truncated list.
Both red stacks are read as two plates each, though the inset only shows one stack being built.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 12: the aft fuselage and four red round plates are consumed. Yellow 2x2 plates were already at zero, so the earlier mismatch on b126 and b127 stands.
Step 7 sets the big white wing plate (54093, with its 6x10 opening) over the middle of the fuselage chain. The ballast shows through the opening. I read it as resting on sections b83, b84 and b85.

The two blue strips along the fuselage walls toward the nose are read as lego-3034 blue 2x8 plates, which matches the count of four in the parts list. They sit on b85 and b86. They could be 1x8 tiles (4162) instead.
The short blue piece near the nose end is read as a blue 1x2 plate, with its type and size uncertain.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 13: the wing plate, two blue 2x8 plates and one blue 1x2 plate are consumed.

Step 8 adds blue strips on the wall ledges of the rear fuselage, two per side, plus a blue 1x2 plate dropped into the gap at the top. The page shows 1-wide strips of different lengths. I read them as the last two 2x8 plates (lego-3034) for the longest ones and two 1x6 plates (lego-3666) for the shorter ones.
Which strip is which size, and which section each sits on, is a best estimate from the drawing's spacing. Both the sizes and the sections are uncertain.
Page 13's nose strips may belong on b86 and the nose b97 instead of b85.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 14: both blue 2x8 plates, two blue 1x6 plates and one blue 1x2 plate are consumed.

Step 9 caps every blue strip with dark bluish gray plates. By area, the plates seem to use up all the dark bluish gray 1x8s, 1x4s and 1x2s in stock (two 3460, five 3710, four 3023). The drawing is too small to see the exact split, so the allocation is a best guess.
Sticker marks appear on the wing in the step 9 drawing. They are from sticker sheet 55075 and are not recorded as parts here.
I counted 4 dark 1x2 plates in stock (3023 DBG) but placed only four, with b140, b145, b146 and b147, so the total is right.

Page 16 has no building step. It shows three finished sub-models from booklet 1 (the 5-seat plate, the 6-seat plate and the check-in desk with coffee machine) with lines pointing to the next page. They are probably shown as modules that go into the airplane's cabin. Nothing new is added.

Correction to page 15: the remaining-parts diff shows that page consumed only two 1x8 dark bluish gray plates, one dark bluish gray 1x4 plate and four blue 1x2 plates. The four dark 1x2 plates were not used, as the list still shows 4, and nor were the other four dark 1x4 plates. My page 15 split of dark plates over the nose and lower strips (b139 to b147) is therefore wrong in part. Only b137 and b138 (the two 1x8s) and one dark 1x4 are confirmed, and the dark strips probably need to be rechecked against the following pages.

Step 10 adds no new pieces, as the remaining-parts list is unchanged from page 16. The three modules built in booklet 1 are placed into the fuselage, shown by the arrows from page 16: the 5-seat plate (b12) at the rear, the 6-seat plate (b5) in the wing opening, and the desk-and-coffee-machine plate (b21) in the forward section.
Which fuselage sections each plate sits on is estimated from the picture. Each plate spans two sections, so it is joined to two.
Page 16's earlier note still applies: the page 15 dark strip allocations (b139 to b147) are unreliable.
Step 11 adds two light bluish gray 75° slopes (2x box) in the nose section on each side of the cockpit doorway, resting on the nose and the blue strips.

Four white 1x2x2 bricks (3245b) go onto the wing plate around the opening: two on the rear side of the opening, one of them already shown seated and one at the nose end of the opening. This matches the four 3245b left in stock. The drawing shows three already seated and one with arrows dropping in. The exact positions are best guesses.
No pins or other joins are shown on this page.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 18: the four 3245b bricks and two 4460a slopes are consumed.

Step 12 (18x) places eighteen white 1x4x2 windows (4863), each with two trans-brown glass panes (4862), along both sides of the fuselage. Nine are assigned to each side. That is 36 panes. Step 12 (2x) puts two white 1x2x2 windows (2377) with one pane each on top of the two nose slopes, which gives 38 panes, the full count in the parts list.

Which window sits on which strip or wing stretch is estimated from the picture. The wing plate's edge studs carry many of the middle windows, so those are listed as resting on b128, with the blue strips used where they show underneath.
Glass panes are not clutched to anything, so they are listed with nothing resting under them and joined to their window frames.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 19: the eighteen 1x4x2 windows, two 1x2x2 windows and all 38 glass panes are consumed.

Step 13 adds blue 1x6 plates (lego-3666, all five in stock) as roof ties across the fuselage. Two cross the cabin at either end of the wing opening, one crosses the cockpit area, and two run lengthwise at the nose. Two blue 1x2 plates (3023) go on the nose side, with the one at the top shown being pushed on by arrows. The 5 plates are all the blue 1x6s in stock, which fits the diff.
The exact windows each strip rests on are estimated from the picture and could be off by a window or two.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 20: all five blue 1x6 plates and both blue 1x2 plates are consumed.
Step 14: the cockpit module built on page 5 (plate b44 and its pieces) is set into the aft end of the fuselage, shown by the inset arrow.

This page also shows blue grooved tiles capping the tops of the windows, with one being lowered by arrows on the far side. These are read as 1x8 (4162) and 1x6 (6636) tiles. The drawing is too small to tell how many there are, so I recorded three of each, and the rest (two of each in stock) are presumably placed on later pages.
Which windows each tile covers is a best estimate.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 21: three blue 1x8 tiles and three blue 1x6 tiles are consumed.

Step 15 uses the last blue grooved tiles, two 1x8 (4162) and two 1x6 (6636), at the rear end of the cabin. One 1x8 is shown being lowered by arrows onto the far-side windows. The other three cap the near-side windows and the rear end.
Piece sizes and the windows they rest on are best estimates from the rear-end view.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 22: both blue 1x8 tiles and both blue 1x6 tiles are consumed.

Step 16 (2x) pushes a light bluish gray 4L bar into a stud on the floor plate in each cabin. One goes in the rear cabin on the 5-seat plate (b12) and one in the forward cabin beside the desk (b21). The bars are read as lego-30374. They are held by a stud clutch, so they are listed as resting on those plates.
A pilot minifigure sits in the cockpit seat and another stands in the forward cabin in the drawing. Minifigure parts are not in the parts list, so they are not recorded.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 23: both light bluish gray 4L bars are consumed.

Step 17 caps the two ends of the cabin with the two white curved slopes with cutouts (54096), one over the cockpit end and one over the other end. Each has a door or window cutout. The drawing shows a printed bird and windscreen on the left end, which come from the large printed fuselage pieces already placed.

Which pieces each shell rests on is estimated from the drawing. Earlier notes identified the two big printed fuselage ends as b97 (54092) and b121 (54701). The page 9 and 12 diffs confirm those part numbers, but the cockpit-window end on this page looks like the one I called b121, so the two end-piece labels may be swapped. I left them as recorded.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 24: both 54096 slopes are consumed.

Step 18 builds the cabin roof from the three white curved 8x8x2 bricks (54095). The arrows show four black Technic pins, two at each joint. The three-piece roof is then lowered onto the fuselage between the two end shells.
The roof pieces are read as lego-54095, the only three white curved bricks in stock. What each roof section rests on is estimated, since they bridge the blue tie bars and tiles on both sides.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 25: three white curved 8x8x2 bricks and four Technic pins are consumed.

Step 19 (2x) builds two curved doors (54097), each with a light bluish gray arm (30377) in its hinge bracket, and hangs one in each end shell's door opening. The doors carry printed EXIT and blue-stripe artwork, which is not a part.
Step 1 may show two arms per door, but only three arms (30377) are in stock for two doors, so I recorded one per door. The next page's diff should show whether the third arm was used.
Page 27 starts booklet 3, the wings and engines. The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 26: both doors and two of the three arms are consumed, so one arm per door.

Step 20 and its inset build one engine axle assembly that crosses the fuselage roof. The block is a grey 2x4 plate carrying a yellow plate and black plate(s), with a Technic pin out of each end. A large engine cylinder goes on each pin, and a grey undercarriage stand (42608) at each outer end sits on the wing plate.

I could only identify one black end plate (2444, the last in stock). The drawing seems to show black at both ends of the block, but the stock list does not hold a second 2x2 black plate. The yellow plate is read as lego-3021 (2x3), the only fitting yellow plate left, and the block's exact make-up is uncertain.
Four large engines (43121) are in stock but this step seems to need two. The other two are presumably used later, as are the engine fans.

The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 27: the last black 2x2 plate, the 2x4 plate, yellow 2x3 plate, two 43121 engines, two 42608 stands and two pins are consumed. It also confirms the engine axle assembly b244 to b252.

Step 21 (2x) builds the two main landing-gear legs. Each has a pair of dark pylon connectors joined by a Technic pin. The pair is set on a light grey plate. Under that plate sits a 2x2 wheel holder (4870) that carries two wheels with tyres. The plate is clutched to the wing next to the engines.

Parts-count problems: the two legs together need four 32530 pylons, but only three were left in stock. Both legs also need a light grey plate, and only one 3020 and one 3795 were left, so I used 3020 for one leg and 3795 for the other. The 'dark pylon' pieces may be a mix of 32530 and 75535. The next page's diff should show which.

The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 28 with corrections: all three 32530 pylons were used (not four), plus both a 3020 and a 3795 plate. The page 28 gear-plate colour guesses may be off. The 3795 plate consumed there is listed as yellow in stock, so b265 may really be a yellow 3795 or another plate.

Step 22 builds the nose gear. A dark bluish gray 2x2 pin tile (2460) gets a Technic bush on its pin, and a tan axle pin is pushed into the bush. The tile is lowered onto a 2x2 wheel holder (4870) that carries two wheels with tyres. The axle pin goes up into the nose end of the fuselage.
Which end shell (b231 or b232) the nose gear attaches to is not certain. I chose the cockpit end b231.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 29: the pin tile, a bush, the tan axle pin, a wheel holder, two wheels and two tyres are consumed.

Page 30 builds four identical jet engine pods (4x). Per engine: a black 4-prong bar (2566) fitted with four Technic bushes and a red round plate, a white 2x2x2 cone (3942c) on the red plate, and the core pushed into a large light bluish gray nacelle (43121). A black fan (46667) goes into the nacelle's front. A white fairing, a white inverted slope (3747b) plus a white curved 6x2 brick (44126), sits on top of the nacelle.

Parts-count problems: only two 43121 nacelles and three red 4032a plates are left in stock, but four of each are needed here. I recorded four engines as the manual shows. The page 27 axle assembly may have used different cylinders than the 43121s it consumed.

In inset steps 1–2 the fairing sits on a blue plate. No stock part matches it (all blue 2x8s, 1x6s and 1x4s are used up), so I left it out and the fairing is recorded as resting on the nacelle only. The blue plate is probably a part I mis-assigned on an earlier page.
Only the engine sub-assemblies are recorded here. The arrow at the bottom right points to later pages that mount them on the wings.
Step 23 adds no new pieces. The four engine pods built on page 30 are pressed onto the wing, two per wing, by their white fairings. The picture shows the plane upside down.

The diff after page 30 shows all four 2566 bars, four cones, four fans and four fairing pairs consumed. But it shows only two 43121 nacelles and three red 4032a plates consumed, plus 15 bushes. So page 30's engine builds cannot all have used a 43121 and a red plate each, or my page 27 and page 30 assignments of 43121 are mixed up. The fix would be to treat two of the 'nacelles' as the cylinders on the page 27 axle.

A blue plate shows under each engine fairing in this view. No blue plate of a matching type is left in stock. I think I mis-assigned some blue 2x8 or 1x6 plates on pages 13–15, so the blue plates under the engine fairings are not recorded here.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 31: no new pieces were consumed, so only the engines were moved. The stock was unchanged.

Step 24 (2x) builds two wing flaps, one for each wing tip. Each flap is a white 1x4 hinge plate (44568) clipped to a white 3x4 hinge plate (44570), with two round 2x2 plates (2654) with rounded bottoms pressed into the 1x4 hinge plate. The inset step 1 appears to show white 1x4 plates, but no white 3710 plates are left in stock, so I read them as the hinge plates.
The 1x4 hinge plate of each flap is attached to the wing near the wing tip, and the 3x4 plate hinges up and down.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 32: four 2654 dishes and both hinge-plate pairs are consumed.

Step 25 adds the blue printed tail fin (54094pr0001) on the tail end of the fuselage, the left and right white 6x12 wedge plates (30355 and 30356) as the horizontal stabilisers on the tail piece's side plates, and a white 8x8 cut-corner wedge plate (30504) on each wing-tip flap (the flap hinge plates from page 32).
Which end piece carries the tail is uncertain. I put the tail and stabilisers on b97 and b232. The page 24 note about the end pieces possibly being swapped still applies.
The 'remaining parts' diff backs up page 33: the tail, both stabilisers and both 8x8 wedge plates are consumed.

Step 26 adds three navigation lights as round 1x1 plates. The trans-clear one goes on a white jumper plate (3794a, a 1x2 plate with one centred stud) on the tail fin top. The trans-green one goes on the left wing-tip triangle, and the trans-red one on the right wing-tip triangle.
The white piece on the tail top could be a 1x2 tile, but a tile has no stud for the light, so I read it as the white 3794a jumper that is still in stock.

Page 35 has no building step. It shows the finished airplane with the yellow stair truck (built on pages 6–7) beside the open cabin door, a minifigure on the stairs and a worker minifigure holding the two wands (b1 to b4) in the corner. The 'LC 7893' sticker is shown on the fuselage and is not recorded as a part.

Stock mismatch with page 34: the page 34 diff shows three blue 6141 round plates and the black jumper plate consumed, while the three trans-coloured 6141s and the white jumper are still listed as unplaced. The drawing clearly shows green, red and clear/grey lights, so I recorded b336 to b339 as seen. If the diff is right, b336 should be the black 3794a and b337 to b339 should be blue 6141s, so those colours/types may need correcting.
The parts list still shows tyres, wheels, wheel holders, arms, clips and other small parts unplaced. They are probably for the remaining pages, such as the second stair truck and the baggage cart.
Page 36 is a full-colour parts inventory with element numbers and quantities. It has no building step, so nothing is added.

The inventory confirms the element numbers for the main parts, for example the nose fuselage 4288459, the rear fuselage 4288451, the tail 4288464, the wing plate 4284004, the curved bricks 4284006 and the curved slopes 4284007.

Page 37 is the second page of the full-colour parts inventory, with element numbers and quantities, mostly minifigure parts, black and grey parts and the Technic pieces. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Page 38 is an advertising and customer-service page (a 'Win LEGO products' survey notice and contact numbers). It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Page 39 is advertising for the LEGO Club magazine and the LEGO Shop at Home catalogue. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Page 40 is the back-cover advertisement for the LEGO City range (sets 7890, 7891, 7892, 7893, 7894, 7901, 7902 and 7903). It has no building step, so nothing is added.

Parts left unplaced by the end, from the last remaining list: the white 1x2 grille tile and 1x2 tile, the black 4x4 plate, the arm, the sloped flight-controls brick, two white 2x2 tiles, tyres, wheels and wheel holders, three turntable tops, dark bluish gray plates, the jumper, 2x6 plate, clips, briefcase, cones, panels, a tap, the 54090 bottom fuselage and the sticker sheet. The model I recorded uses everything else, but 54090 was never seen as a placed step, which suggests the end pieces on pages 9 and 12 may have been the wrong parts. Some of these leftovers are spare parts, and a few may belong to the stair truck, baggage cart or minifigure props shown on the cover and on page 35 but never given building steps in the pages I saw.
Additions only, as requested. Nothing already given has been changed or removed.

L4 missing parts: I added every part still unplaced in the last remaining-parts list (b340 to b394). No building step for them appears in the pages I was given, so they are probably spares, extra accessories or steps not in the sequence. Only the spare wheel sets are joined, as two holders with four wheels and four tyres. The rest stay free-standing. The trans-coloured 6141 round plates are listed because the diffs say the pieces placed on page 34 were really blue 6141s and a black jumper. So b337 to b339 should be read as blue 6141s, and b336 as the black 3794a. The new b367 is the white 3794a.

L4 over-counts that I cannot remove with additions only. These existing ids should be retyped or dropped by whoever merges: b126 and b127 (3022 yellow, none were left; they are really yellow caps of another type), b263 (a fourth 32530; only three exist), b317 (a fifth 4032a; only seven exist), b316 (a seventeenth 3713; only 16 exist), and two of the engine nacelles, b308 and b319 (43121; only four exist and two were already used on page 27). The diff after page 30 shows only two nacelles, three red plates and fifteen bushes were really consumed.

L3 groups: the graph has separate models by design. The stair truck (b63 to b81), the two wands (b1 and b2, b3 and b4) and the airplane are different toys in this set. The wands are held by a minifigure's hands, and minifigure parts are not in the parts list. I added one contact link (b72 to b240) because page 35 shows the stair truck parked against the plane's door. The wands cannot be linked to anything.

L5 tile-rests: these are not real stacking errors in the manual. b35 (the coffee-machine box) sits on the two grille tiles b25 and b26 together with the blue and slope parts beside it, as shown on page 4. b231 sits on b228 and b233 sits on b219, b222 and b225 because the roof shells and roof sections sit on the window rows. The blue tiles only cap those rows, and the real clutch is on the windows' studs, which I listed as other 'rests_on' entries. b234 sits on b221 and b224 for the same reason. b272 (the Technic bush) is not stacked on the tile b271 at all. It slides over the tile's top pin, as the existing join b272 to b271 states. I could not drop the extra rests_on entries, so please treat those as geometric contact, not clutch.
Additions only. Nothing already given has been changed or removed.

L3 groups: the many loose groups came from the spare parts I added last time. They were not placed in any step on the 40 pages I was given. I have now joined them to the model: the turntable tops go onto their bases; the clip plates, bars, arm, bag, pins and connectors form one accessory cluster on the spare black 4x4 plate; the spare 2x6 plate with the yellow panels and dark plates forms a second cluster; the four extra tyres, wheels and holders are linked as wheel sets; the white tap and slope, tiles and jumper sit on the desk plate; the 54090 bottom half is joined to the nose end; and the sticker sheet is joined to the fuselage. The clusters are placed by guess, and the contact edges to the stair truck are only 'lying nearby'. Treat the cluster contents and positions as best guesses, because the booklet pages given show no step for them.

Still separate by design: the two wands (b1 and b2, b3 and b4). They are separate hand-held props that the worker minifigure holds, and minifigure parts are not in the parts list.
